correctness.rationale: Koponen's tuple equivalence records a tournament diagram exactly up to one global edge reversal, and overlapping triples force a single preserve-or-reverse mode for any automorphism of the reduct. Hence the automorphism group is the known automorphism/anti-automorphism group. An anti-automorphism can be arranged to fix zero or one named point, but none can fix two distinct points because their directed edge would have to reverse while both endpoints remain fixed. Omega-categoricity therefore gives the exact two-parameter definability threshold. For the type formula, equality patterns with k new classes are counted by inclusion-exclusion, every orientation bit is realized by the random-tournament extension property, and global complement halves the orientations exactly when at most one parameter is fixed. Fresh formula replay reproduces the displayed type counts.
risks: The proof uses the standard omega-categorical orbit-definability correspondence; no formal proof assistant certificate is supplied.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the exact finite parameter threshold at which a canonical homogeneous reduct recovers its hidden binary orientation and packages the consequence into a closed complete-type spectrum. This is a natural invariant of a standard reduct, not an arbitrary small computation.
risks: Only the global-converse reduct is covered, not the switching reducts.

final_claim: For Koponen's global-converse reduct of the countable random tournament, the hidden tournament orientation is not definable over zero or one parameter but is definable over every pair of distinct parameters; this symmetry break yields the stated exact finite-parameter complete-type formula and orbit profiles.
limitations: Real finite parameter sets only; no imaginary or infinite-parameter types.
